Subject: Post-demo: data handling / subprocessor details (PII, retention, telemetry)

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Wanted to follow up with a short recap and next steps on the data/privacy items you flagged so your security and legal teams can triage.

Recap / clarifications from our side:
- PII handling: Redwood does not use customer prompt/content data to train models. Any customer data stored for routing/observability is encrypted at rest.
- Retention: Default logging retention is 90 days; we can configure shorter retention windows for enterprise contracts (30/7 days) and support secure deletion on request.
- Logging controls: Access to logs is RBAC-protected; we offer token-level tracing for debugging but can disable token-level payloads and only keep meta telemetry.
- Data residency: Hosted API runs in region-specific clusters (US, EU). For strict residency we offer Dedicated or Private deployments.
- Third-party sharing / subprocessors: We use cloud providers (AWS, GCP) and telemetry vendors (Sentry/Datadog for ops, Segment for anonymous usage metrics) — we can share a current subprocessor inventory.

Next steps I proposed on the call:
1) I attach our current subprocessor inventory (pdf). Please share with your InfoSec/legal.
2) Can you send over Acme Health's security questionnaire or specify the highest-priority questions (PII retention, vendor list, encryption, SOC2 artifacts)?
3) If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min follow-up with Dylan (security/infra owner) to walk through telemetry and cloud-provider controls.

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory.pdf

Proposed times for the follow-up: Wed 3/17 9:30–10:00 or Thu 3/18 10:00–10:30 (PT) — let us know what works.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the attachment. A few quick clarifications from our side:
- We consider any free-text patient notes PII and need an assurance they won't be used for model training. Good to hear Redwood already avoids that.
- Retention: 90 days is our standard max; for PHI-related logs we likely need a 30-day or shorter option. Would you confirm configurable retention windows are in contractable controls?
- Telemetry: we need a list of telemetry vendors and confirmation that telemetry is pseudonymized (no patient identifiers).
- Cloud provider: Please confirm which regions/internal regions the hosted API uses (we're primarily concerned about data being stored in the US-only).

I've attached our security questionnaire (high level) — legal will review the subprocessor inventory and follow up with redlines. For the follow-up call, Wed 3/17 9:30 PT works for our infra lead.

Attachment: Acme_Health_SecQ.pdf

Samantha —

Appreciate the quick turn. Quick answers inline and attached a more detailed subprocessor export for your legal team (redwood-subprocessors-2026Q1.pdf):

- Training data: Confirmed — we do NOT use customer prompts or responses to train or fine-tune public models. Any optional feedback you choose to provide for quality improvement is opt-in and can be compartmentalized per contract.
- Retention windows: Yes — retention is configurable and contractable. We offer 90/30/7-day options for request payloads and logs; for PHI workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private where retention controls are enforced at deployment.
- Telemetry vendors: We use Datadog for infra metrics, Sentry for error traces (payloads stripped by default), and Segment for anonymous usage metrics. All telemetry is configured to strip PII; we can provide the configuration snippets and SOC2 controls.
- Cloud regions: Hosted API runs on multi-cloud US clusters (us-west-2, us-east-1) for low latency. If Acme requires US-only residency and contractual guarantees, Dedicated or Private is the recommended path.

Next steps:
- I'll share the detailed subprocessor export (attached) for legal review.
- Dylan can join the Wed 3/17 9:30 PT slot to walk infra controls — cc'd.
- If legal has specific redlines we can route to our legal team; deal contact is me and I can loop in contracts after initial redlines.

Attachments: redwood-subprocessors-2026Q1.pdf

Best,
Marissa
